nodes.description: Mild cerebellar involvement, inferred from the oculomotor signs and dysarthria in the Dutch family. Pld3 knockout mice show no Purkinje cell loss, no cerebellar atrophy and normal rotarod performance, and PLD3 expression is lowest in the adult cerebellum of all brain regions, so a direct effect of PLD3 loss on the cerebellum is unsupported in mice.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline missense variant, PLD3 c.923T>C p.(Leu308Pro), in the second phosphodiesterase domain, found by exome sequencing in the Dutch family. It is the only variant with family segregation data. A different variant, p.(Ile26Thr), was reported in one Indian patient without segregation or zygosity data.

nodes.description: PLD3 is the main acid 5' exonuclease in cultured cells, and its major physiological substrate is mitochondrial DNA. In PLD3-deficient neurons and cell lines, mtDNA builds up in lysosomes and leaks into the cytosol, where it activates cGAS-STING signalling. These consequences come from PLD3-deficient cells studied in an Alzheimer's disease context; none has been shown in SCA46 patients or tested for the L308P variant, so the node records the expected cellular result of losing PLD3 exonuclease activity.

evidence.snippet: Lysosomal leakage of mtDNA to the cytosol activates cGAS-STING signaling that upregulates autophagy and induces amyloid precursor C-terminal fragment (APP-CTF) and cholesterol accumulation.

nodes.description: Axonal degeneration of myelinated sensory fibres, shown on sural nerve biopsy in the Dutch family, producing a sensory polyneuropathy. Whether the primary lesion is in dorsal root ganglion neurons has not been examined. The pathology is established in patients; its link to PLD3 is not.

evidence.reference_title: A new variant of sensory ataxic neuropathy with autosomal dominant inheritance.
evidence.snippet: Clinical, electrophysiological and sural nerve biopsy findings revealed a sensory polyneuropathy due to axonal degeneration of myelinated nerve fibres in four of five investigated siblings.

nodes.description: Wild-type PLD3 travels to lysosomes as a type II transmembrane protein by an ESCRT-dependent route and is cleaved there into a stable soluble enzyme. In transfected cells the L308P protein instead accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum, is barely processed and has no 5' exonuclease activity. These results come from overexpression in cell lines, not from patient cells.

meta.association: Provisional and disputed. The association rests on one Dutch family with the heterozygous p.Leu308Pro variant. Pld3 knockout mice have no cerebellar phenotype, and the group that generated them questioned PLD3 as the SCA46 gene; a reply from the original authors was published (PMID:30312384). One further patient carries a different variant, with no segregation data and an unremarkable family history.

nodes.description: PLD3 also synthesizes S,S-bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a lysosomal phospholipid needed to degrade lipids such as gangliosides. Pld3 deletion lowers brain BMP in mice. In transfected cells the L308P protein reached lysosomes poorly, was poorly processed and did not raise BMP levels, so the variant loses this function too. Whether reduced BMP contributes to neuropathy or ataxia in patients is unknown.

evidence.reference_title: PLD3 and PLD4 synthesize S,S-BMP, a key phospholipid enabling lipid degradation in lysosomes.
evidence.snippet: Deletion of PLD3 or PLD4 markedly reduced BMP levels in cells or in murine tissues where either enzyme is highly expressed (brain for PLD3; spleen for PLD4), leading to gangliosidosis and lysosomal abnormalities.
